@make-proposal-agent RT-APEX-001 — Treasury feasibility assessment (analysis only; no approval, reservation, or settlement)

Arithmetic:
- Proposed internal delivery limit: 90,000 USD cents.
- Allocations: Research 10,000 + Design 20,000 + Development 45,000 + QA 15,000 = 90,000 cents.
- Assumed base cost: 30h × 2,500 cents/h = 75,000 cents.
- Proposed contingency: 15,000 cents; 75,000 + 15,000 = 90,000 cents.
- Indicative gross margin: 150,000 − 90,000 = 60,000 cents; 60,000 / 150,000 = 40%. Delivery budget consumes 60% of stated revenue.

Feasibility:
The arithmetic is internally consistent. The proposal is only conditionally feasible: 90,000 cents is a proposed ceiling based on unverified rate, hours, scope caps and client-funded third-party services. The 40% figure is a budget-based projected gross margin, not an actual margin or cash position; it excludes unverified overhead, tax, payment-processing, rework, external services and collection risk.

Limits, capacity and funding:
No authorized read-only backend evidence is available to me. Agreed revenue is not verified as received; available balance, existing commitments, reservations, approval limits, policy status and delivery capacity are all unverified. The 10/20/45/15 allocations should be treated as internal proposed limits, not funds available or commitments. The 15,000-cent contingency is shared headroom, not an automatic entitlement for any workstream.

Financial risks and controls:
1. Do not treat client agreement as cash availability: verify receivable/payment terms, receipt status, taxes/fees and authoritative project funding.
2. Before owner review, reconcile scope, actual internal rates, assigned capacity, supplier/subscription responsibility, commitments and reservations.
3. Keep a hard aggregate ceiling of 90,000 cents; require documented re-estimation and new review/approval for scope expansion, allocation transfer, rate change, or forecast above the ceiling.
4. Track base-cost burn and contingency use separately by workstream; contingency draw requires recorded justification and does not override the aggregate ceiling.
5. Require independent policy review and backend-verified owner authorization bound to the exact project/request revision, recipient, purpose, amount and currency before any simulated settlement.
6. Revalidate request revision, approval validity, policy, balance/commitment state and idempotency controls immediately before any future simulated settlement; reconcile receipt and ledger afterward.

Recommendation:
Financially suitable only as a provisional owner-review proposal after the above facts are verified. It is not ready for spending or operational commitment.

@make-proposal-agent RT-APEX-001 — independent internal cost estimate (analysis only; no approval, reservation, or record created).

POTENTIAL COMMITMENT
Project: RT-APEX-001 / Apex Media
Recipient: Internal delivery team and any separately procured third-party services
Amount: Recommended internal delivery budget 141000 cents
Currency: USD
Purpose: Six-page marketing website under the stated proposed scope caps
Promise date: Unknown
Status: UNVERIFIED LEAD — this is a planning estimate, not an obligation. The 150000-cent revenue is also not verified as received.

EVIDENCE
Source: Current project brief and coordinator’s unverified 30-hour/90000-cent proposal.
Supporting context: Homepage, portfolio (up to six external embeds), three service pages, contact form, responsive implementation, and basic SEO; client supplies content, brand assets, media rights and privacy wording.
Evidence classification: EVIDENCE FOUND for scope description; all rate, effort, subscription, capacity and revenue assumptions remain unverified.

COST MODEL
Assumed blended internal rate: 2500 cents/hour, integer; unverified. This is retained solely for comparability with the original proposal, not asserted as an actual staff cost.

- Research — 4–6h; planning 5h; 12500-cent base. Scope discovery, asset/right and form/hosting/privacy gates, architecture, technical plan. Resource: delivery lead/strategist.
- Design — 8–12h; planning 10h; 25000-cent base. Visual direction, responsive layouts, component/template specification, one proposed revision. Resource: product/web designer.
- Development — 22–30h; planning 24h; 60000-cent base. Template build, six proposed pages, responsive behavior, external video embeds, lead form integration, basic SEO implementation. Resource: web developer.
- QA and handover — 7–10h; planning 8h; 20000-cent base. Cross-browser/mobile, form delivery and validation, embed/load checks, basic SEO checks, one proposed correction round and handover. Resource: QA/delivery lead.

Planning total: 47h (range 41–58h), 117500-cent base cost. Recommended contingency: 23500 cents (20% of base), covering clarification, asset defects, third-party integration behavior and permitted rework. Recommended allocation: Research 12500; Design 25000; Development 60000; QA 20000; shared contingency 23500. Recommended budget: 141000 cents.

RECURRING / EXTERNAL DEPENDENCIES
Hosting, domain, form/email delivery, spam protection, video host availability and any analytics/consent tooling may recur. They are excluded only under the unverified proposal that the client pays them directly. Confirm provider, price, billing owner, data handling, renewal and failure path before work begins.

90000-CENT TRADEOFF
At the same assumed rate, 90000 cents supports only 30h plus no defensible contingency if treated as total spend. It is 51000 cents below the 141000-cent recommendation. To hold a 90000-cent cap, scope must be explicitly reduced: use a prebuilt theme/template, limit bespoke design and QA, make client-owned form/hosting configuration a prerequisite, limit embeds/pages further, and defer nonessential SEO/analytics. Even then, the cap is not validated until actual rates, capacity and third-party charges are confirmed.

VERIFICATION
Potential duplicate: No accessible ledger entries or existing commitment records were supplied; duplicate status unknown. Compare any later commitments by recipient, amount, currency, purpose and source.
Person who can confirm: Budget owner for rate/capacity and any internal commitment; client contact for scope, assets, service ownership and change limits.
Owner confirmation: Not requested and not present.
Backend recording status: Unknown; no backend record was consulted or created.

FINANCIAL IMPACT
Against unverified 150000-cent agreed revenue, the recommended 141000-cent budget leaves a provisional 9000-cent gross margin before overhead, taxes, transaction fees or external services. This is not an authoritative balance or profitability statement.

NEXT ACTION
make-proposal-agent should reconcile this range with the requirements and risk reviews, present the unverified assumptions and 90000-cent tradeoffs to the budget owner, and obtain scope/rate confirmation before any financial workflow.

@make-proposal-agent RT-APEX-001 — requirements analysis (analysis only)

1. Business objective and users
- Objective: present Apex Media professionally, demonstrate production work, explain services, and convert prospective clients into qualified enquiries.
- Primary users: prospective buyers/marketing leads assessing capability and portfolio.
- Secondary users: Apex staff receiving and responding to enquiries; client administrators supplying/approving content.
- Success intent: visitors can understand offerings, view portfolio items, and submit a usable enquiry on mobile or desktop.

2. Confirmed brief requirements
Functional
- Homepage.
- Portfolio.
- Service pages (count/content not stated).
- Lead-capture form.
- Responsive design.
- Basic SEO (scope not stated).
Nonfunctional
- Professional agency presentation.
- Usable across responsive breakpoints.
- Portfolio/video and form must operate reliably.
- SEO implementation must be technically sound within the agreed definition.

3. Proposed scope caps — NOT client requirements
- Six pages: home, portfolio, three services, contact.
- Up to six externally hosted video embeds; single language; reusable templates; no custom CMS.
- Client provides copy, brand assets, media-rights evidence and privacy wording.
- One design revision and one acceptance-defect correction round.
- Hosting/domain/form subscriptions paid separately by client.
- 10 business days after all prerequisites; no start date confirmed.
These caps need explicit client acceptance before becoming contractual scope.

4. Proposed deliverables and dependencies
- Discovery/scope record: approved sitemap, page count, service taxonomy, conversion goal, acceptance plan. Depends on client decisions.
- Design: responsive visual direction and reusable page templates. Depends on brand assets, copy direction, and approved scope.
- Website build: agreed pages, portfolio/video embed implementation, lead form with routing/validation/spam control, responsive styling, metadata/indexing configuration. Depends on approved design, content, platform/hosting credentials and third-party choices.
- QA/handover: cross-device checks, form-delivery evidence, SEO/pre-launch checklist, access/ownership handover. Depends on deployed review environment and client acceptance contact.
- External dependencies: video host availability/embedding permission, media rights, form provider and consent/privacy requirements, domain/DNS/hosting access, email destination.

5. Measurable acceptance criteria (proposed; client must approve)
- Approved sitemap/page inventory is delivered; every approved page is reachable from navigation and has no broken internal links.
- Portfolio contains only the approved number of approved, externally hosted embeds; embeds load or display a graceful fallback on representative mobile and desktop tests.
- Lead form requires agreed fields, rejects invalid submissions, uses agreed anti-spam protection, and one successful test arrives at the nominated inbox.
- Defined responsive test matrix (at minimum one common mobile and one desktop viewport) has no blocking layout or navigation defects.
- Each indexable approved page has unique title and meta description; production robots/indexing choice, canonical/domain and sitemap status match written client instructions.
- No critical launch-blocking defects in agreed browser/device matrix; client records acceptance against these criteria.
- Accessibility, performance, analytics, legal compliance, uptime SLA and content-editing capability are excluded unless explicitly added; if added, they require their own measurable criteria.

6. Missing information and clarification gates
A. Blocking before scope/SOW commitment
- Named client decision-maker and acceptance authority.
- Final page inventory, service-page count, portfolio count, desired navigation, languages, and confirmation whether CMS/content editing is required.
- Form fields, recipient inbox/CRM, spam-control approach, privacy/consent wording, data retention and legal jurisdiction.
- Hosting/domain/DNS owner and access path; delivery platform/technology constraints.
- Exact meaning of “basic SEO”: included metadata, sitemap, robots/indexing, redirects, analytics, keyword/content work, or reporting.
- Brand guidelines/assets, final copy/content owner, portfolio media list, and evidence of rights/permission for all media and embeds.
- Required launch deadline, project start trigger, review cadence, and response-time assumptions.
- Explicit acceptance of scope caps, change-control process, revisions/correction definitions, and treatment of third-party recurring fees.

B. Required before build starts
- Approved design direction and content inventory.
- Working hosting/domain and form/video-provider credentials or documented client-managed alternatives.
- Nominated test/acceptance contacts and deployed review environment.

C. Required before launch/acceptance
- Final content/rights confirmation; approved privacy/legal copy; verified form delivery; production domain/indexing decision; client acceptance record.

7. Key scope controls
- Any extra pages, videos, languages, CMS, custom integrations, analytics/SEO expansion, accessibility target, revisions beyond agreed cap, or client-content production should be separately estimated and approved through change control.
- The stated 30h/10-business-day estimate and financial figures do not establish requirements or readiness.

Clarification gates: Gate 1—written scope and caps accepted; Gate 2—assets/access/legal/form decisions complete; Gate 3—design and build sign-off; Gate 4—launch checklist and recorded client acceptance. No financial or project record has been created or modified.

@make-proposal-agent RT-APEX-001-RISK — independent challenge (analysis only)

Bottom line: NEEDS MORE INFORMATION. The $90,000-cent / 30h / 10-business-day model is a planning hypothesis, not a feasible committed baseline. No authoritative project, capacity, rate, cash-receipt, commitment, or client-approval record was supplied.

Arithmetic corrections:
• Six proposed pages is internally consistent: home + portfolio + three services + contact.
• 30h × 2,500 cents/h = 75,000 cents base; 15,000 cents contingency gives 90,000 cents total.
• Allocations total 90,000 cents. They embed contingency of 2,500 / 2,500 / 7,500 / 2,500 cents across Research / Design / Development / QA, rather than showing it as a controlled reserve. Separate the 75,000-cent base from the 15,000-cent contingency; do not treat either as approved spend.
• A 10-day elapsed window is not supportable without a confirmed start, working capacity, asset readiness, feedback SLA, and launch/acceptance dates. Thirty hours may fit ten days only at ~3 delivery hours/day before coordination and rework; it does not establish a reliable delivery promise.

Risk register:
1. Client scope is incomplete — Severity Critical; Probability High; Impact: page count, CMS, copy, analytics, accessibility, legal and SEO work can expand beyond 30h. Mitigation: signed SOW with inclusions/exclusions, caps and change control. Owner: Research.
2. “Basic SEO” undefined — High/High; Impact: unpriced keyword research, redirects, schema, copy, analytics, Search Console, performance or migration work. Mitigation: define exact SEO deliverables and acceptance metrics. Owner: Research.
3. Asset/copy/rights dependency — High/High; Impact: blocked build, delayed launch, IP exposure and rework. Mitigation: asset manifest, rights evidence, content-ready gate and client feedback SLA. Owner: Research.
4. Lead-form privacy/security/deliverability — Critical/Medium; Impact: personal-data noncompliance, spam, lost leads and unplanned vendor/configuration work. Mitigation: specify fields, recipient inbox, consent/privacy language, retention, spam control, HTTPS and receipt tests before build. Owner: Development.
5. Hosting/domain/form-vendor assumptions — High/Medium; Impact: access delays and costs outside the quote; “client pays” does not prove procurement or access. Mitigation: confirm provider, account owner, credentials, DNS and recurring-cost owner before scheduling. Owner: Research.
6. Video embeds — High/Medium; Impact: external-platform availability, consent/cookie issues, mobile performance and rights constraints can break portfolio acceptance. Mitigation: approved host list, representative URLs, poster/lazy-load approach and device tests. Owner: Development.
7. 30h estimate lacks task-level evidence — High/High; Impact: design system, responsive implementation, content insertion, accessibility, form integration, deployment and handover are likely undercounted. Mitigation: independently bottom-up estimate after scope confirmation; use ranges, not a single point. Owner: Design + Development + QA.
8. Revision limits are unaccepted — High/High; Impact: informal feedback cycles consume contingency and delay handover. Mitigation: written one-revision/one-correction definition, response windows and paid change process. Owner: Design.
9. Sequential handoffs compress the claimed window — High/Medium; Impact: Research → Design → Development → QA leaves little slack; 15h development and 5h QA are not validated for six responsive pages plus integration. Mitigation: capacity-confirmed milestone plan with explicit client gates and schedule contingency. Owner: Delivery/QA.
10. Quality/acceptance criteria absent — High/High; Impact: disputes over browser support, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, form receipt and SEO completion. Mitigation: measurable test matrix and acceptance sign-off criteria. Owner: QA.
11. Financial basis is unverified — High/Medium; Impact: 2,500 cents/h, resource availability, tax/overhead treatment and $1,500 revenue receipt are not evidence; apparent 60,000-cent gross margin excludes overhead/taxes and may not be collectible. Mitigation: owner verifies rates, capacity, payment terms, taxes and receipt status separately from delivery approval. Owner: Finance/Owner.
12. Contingency governance is missing — Medium/High; Impact: embedded 15,000 cents can be silently consumed by normal work, masking an overrun. Mitigation: track base effort against 75,000 cents and require owner change control before contingency use. Owner: Project control.

Explicit blockers before a delivery commitment:
• Client confirmation of scope, CMS/no-CMS choice, page/embed caps, language, revisions and exclusions.
• Content/brand/media-rights package and named decision-maker with feedback timing.
• Form, privacy, hosting/domain/DNS and deployment ownership/access decisions.
• Defined SEO, accessibility, analytics, browser/device and acceptance requirements.
• Independently validated capacity, rates and bottom-up estimate; owner validation of financial assumptions.
• Confirmed start and client deadline. None was supplied.

Recommendation: do not present 10 business days or 90,000 cents as a committed offer. Rebaseline only after the blockers are resolved; if requirements remain as broad as stated, retain a range and change-control mechanism rather than endorsing 30h.

@treasury-ops-agent RT-APEX-001-FIN-R2 reconciliation: all four assessments received. Independent cost specialist estimates 47h planning (41–58h range) at unverified 2500 cents/h: base117500 +20% contingency23500 = proposed141000 cents. Four proposed limits with separately tracked embedded contingency: Research15000 (base12500+2500), Design30000 (25000+5000), Development72000 (60000+12000), QA24000 (20000+4000). Sum141000; revenue150000; projected margin9000 (6%). Range with20% contingency123000–174000, so high case loses24000 before overhead. Please give actual revised financial assessment, including recommendation whether owner should approve this or defer/re-scope/reprice; no financial action. I propose NEEDS_CLIENT_CLARIFICATION with financial review also blocking execution; retain90000 only as unvalidated reduced-scope alternative, not unchanged scope.

@commitment-intelligence-agent RT-APEX-001-COST-R2: Your47h/141000-cent estimate conflicts materially with original30h/90000; I will adopt it as provisional full-scope planning baseline and disclose range123000–174000 with20% contingency. Please confirm four allocations15000/30000/72000/24000 (base12500/25000/60000/20000 plus separately tracked contingency2500/5000/12000/4000). Arithmetic clarification:90000 at2500 cents/h buys36h if zero contingency, or30h plus15000 reserve, rather than only30h with no contingency. Please confirm correction. Proposed schedule15 business days after prerequisites, subject to at least4 productive delivery hours/day across handoffs and client feedback within2 business days; no committed start/deadline. Is this a reasonable conditional estimate? No spending approval requested.

RT-APEX-001: All four specialists have returned substantive assessments. The independent estimate is 47 hours and a proposed $1,410 budget, versus the original 30 hours and $900. That leaves only $90 projected gross margin before overhead and taxes. I’m reconciling the revised allocations and financial assessment; scope, rates, capacity and client dependencies remain unverified.

@make-proposal-agent RT-APEX-001-COST-R2 — confirmed with correction.

The proposed allocations reconcile: Research 15000 (12500 base +2500 contingency); Design 30000 (25000 +5000); Development 72000 (60000 +12000); QA 24000 (20000 +4000) = 117500-cent base +23500-cent contingency = 141000 cents. The 41–58h range at the unverified 2500-cent rate, with 20% contingency, is 123000–174000 cents.

Correction accepted: 90000 cents buys 36h at 2500 cents/hour if no contingency is retained. The original model instead allocates 30h/75000-cent base plus a 15000-cent reserve. My earlier wording was imprecise; it should not state that 90000 supports only 30h with no contingency.

A 15-business-day schedule is a reasonable conditional planning estimate for the 47h baseline only after all prerequisites are complete, assigned capacity is confirmed, a four-productive-hours/day cross-handoff assumption holds, and client feedback is returned within two business days. It is not a delivery commitment: the 41–58h range, clarification gates, unavailable start date, external access and any feedback delay can extend it.

@make-proposal-agent RT-APEX-001-FIN-R2 — Revised treasury assessment (analysis only; no approval or financial action)

Reconciled arithmetic:
- Base: 47h × 2,500 cents/h = 117,500 cents.
- Contingency: 23,500 cents = 20% of base.
- Total proposed planning budget: 141,000 cents.
- Allocation check: 15,000 + 30,000 + 72,000 + 24,000 = 141,000 cents. Their stated bases total 117,500 and their allocation-level contingency portions total 23,500, so the arithmetic is consistent. Track the contingency portions separately even if allocated by workstream.
- Against unverified 150,000-cent revenue: 9,000-cent projected gross margin, or 6%.
- Low range: 41h × 2,500 × 1.20 = 123,000 cents; provisional margin 27,000 cents / 18%.
- High range: 58h × 2,500 × 1.20 = 174,000 cents; provisional loss 24,000 cents / 16%.
All margin figures exclude unverified overhead, taxes, collection risk, payment fees, and third-party charges.

Financial conclusion:
The 141,000-cent point estimate is not a prudent approval baseline for the stated, still-unconfirmed scope. A 6% pre-overhead margin is too thin to absorb remaining uncertainty, and the credible planning range already crosses revenue. Revenue is not verified received; backend balances, commitments, reservations, approval limits, policy status and delivery capacity remain unverified.

Recommendation:
Adopt NEEDS_CLIENT_CLARIFICATION and FINANCIAL_REVIEW_BLOCKS_EXECUTION. Do not recommend owner approval of a 141,000-cent delivery commitment or a 90,000-cent unchanged-scope budget now. Defer for a client-confirmed scope and either:
1. re-scope to a documented reduced-scope package that is independently re-estimated and retains an agreed risk margin; or
2. reprice/restructure client terms to cover the validated full-scope estimate, overhead/fees/taxes, and a defined margin.
The original 90,000-cent figure may be retained only as an unvalidated reduced-scope scenario—not as a full-scope equivalent or spending limit.

Required gates before any later owner-review:
- Client accepts page/embed counts, CMS/language/revision boundaries, SEO definition, acceptance criteria, and change control.
- Hosting/domain/form/video/privacy providers, billing owner, recurring fees, rights, access, and launch dependencies are confirmed.
- Actual rate, staffed capacity, payment/collection terms, authoritative project funding, balance, commitments, reservations, policy result and approval limits are verified.
- Revised estimate separates base, contingency, overhead/external costs, and margin; set aggregate and workstream ceilings plus documented contingency-draw/change-control rules.
- Any eventual approval must be backend-verified and bound to the exact request revision, recipient, purpose, amount and currency.

No backend evidence was consulted or modified; no funds are available by inference.
